Fund the work

Fedimint Card is built by a very small team and paid for out of pocket. Here is what the next stretch needs, how to send sats toward it, and where every sat went.

  • Lightning, on-chain, or a grant
  • Every receipt listed below
  • MIT, whatever happens

What it pays for

32-slot cards are in production on one federation. The gap between that and a card other communities can trust is a list of specific jobs, each with a price. Donations go to the first unfunded item on this list, in order.

  • Independent security review of the applet, the till, and the registry. No one outside the project has reviewed the code. The first review will change it, so it comes before cards reach more hands. Unfunded.
  • Offline payments to production. Applet 3.0 signs offline and has passed staging drills. Taking it to production means a registry migration, a rehearsed restore, and encrypted notes so the registry stops seeing balances. Unfunded.
  • Rotating the chip maker's default management keys. Today anyone with a reader can delete the applet from a card. Per-card keys close that, and need a provisioning change and a key custody plan. Unfunded.
  • Printed card runs and tills for new federations. Blank cards cost $6 to $12 each in small lots. A run of 500 printed cards and a few tills puts the card in the hands that will find the next problem. Unfunded.
  • Development time. The applet, host, registry, and apps are maintained by people who need to eat. A month of funded time is a month of fixes shipped. Unfunded.

Costs are posted here as quotes come in. When an item is funded, it says so here and the receipts appear under Where it went.

Grants and larger gifts

Foundations and companies that want to fund a whole line item, such as the security review, can write to hi@fedimintcard.org. We will send a one-page scope with the deliverable, the reviewer or vendor, the timeline, and what gets published at the end. Reviews and test reports funded this way are published in full in the repository.

The work so far was carried by grants from The Reynolds Foundation and the Human Rights Foundation under Project Island Resilience, and by Flash and Island Bitcoin.

Other ways to help

  • Break it. Audit the applet, host, and registry, and report what you find through a GitHub security advisory or to hi@fedimintcard.org.
  • Build on it. Port the till, add card support to a wallet, or harden the registry. The developer page has the parts and the payment flow.
  • Issue cards. Run cards on your own federation with a till and the Setup app, load small amounts, and tell us what fails.
  • Talk about it. Questions and ideas go in GitHub issues.

Fedimint Card is an independent open source project built on the Fedimint protocol, released under the MIT License. Contact: hi@fedimintcard.org
